claims.explanation: Vinorelbine is a tubulin-polymerization inhibitor, so selectivity is most likely driven by the cellular context that determines mitotic dependence and drug efflux/response rather than by a single lineage. The pattern of sensitive lines is enriched for TP53 pathway loss and for RAS/BRAF-driven tumors with high proliferative signaling, while several resistant lines carry EGFR mutations or intact p53/PTEN contexts that may reduce mitotic vulnerability or increase survival signaling. Features such as TP53 mutation, KRAS/BRAF activation, and high TUBB3 or ABCB1 expression are plausible predictors of response across unseen lines.

features.basis: TP53 mutations are highly enriched in the most-killed lines and loss of p53-mediated arrest increases mitotic catastrophe after tubulin inhibition
KRAS-mutant lines (PATU8988T, NCIH1792, LS1034) are among the most sensitive, consistent with RAS-driven mitotic dependency
BRAF-mutant melanoma/thyroid/endometrial lines (WM793, IGR37, 8305C, HEC265) are enriched among sensitive lines
High TUBB3 (class III beta-tubulin) is a known mediator of resistance to tubulin-binding agents such as vinorelbine
ABCB1/P-glycoprotein efflux reduces intracellular vinorelbine and is a canonical resistance mechanism for vinca alkaloids
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) appear among the least affected, suggesting EGFR signaling supports survival under microtubule stress
PTEN loss co-occurs in several sensitive lines (WM793, HEC265, ZR751) and may impair survival signaling after mitotic stress
CDKN2A loss appears in sensitive lines (KELLY, 8305C, MHHES1) and may compromise cell-cycle checkpoints
ATM mutations appear in sensitive lines (8305C, SNU685) and may reduce DNA-damage responses to mitotic stress
ARID1A mutations are enriched in sensitive lines (HEC265, KU1919, KYSE70, EFE184), possibly reflecting chromatin-remodeling vulnerability
NF1 loss in S117 and other RAS-pathway-activated lines may increase mitotic dependence
MET alterations in HGC27 and 8305C are among sensitive lines, suggesting RTK-driven proliferation increases sensitivity
